species.name: Green Sea Turtle
species.subtitle: Penyu agar · Chelonia mydas
species.intro: Nests on Malaysian beaches. Adults graze on seagrass.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Green turtles forage in shallow coastal waters and seagrass meadows; females nest on sandy beaches.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: They can swallow plastic or become tangled in discarded gear, but this page does not document an injured turtle here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic off the beach, report lost gear, and watch turtles from a distance.

species.name: Dugong
species.subtitle: Dugong dugon
species.intro: Feeding trails have been documented in Sibu–Tinggi seagrass meadows since 2014.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Dugongs graze in shallow seagrass meadows; feeding trails have been recorded around Sibu–Tinggi.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Marine debris and fishing gear can harm dugongs, but the local record is of feeding, not injury.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep waste out of the sea and report lost gear without approaching a dugong.

species.credit: Photo · Jerome Paillet / IFREMER · CC BY 4.0

species.name: Giant Mudskipper
species.subtitle: Periophthalmodon schlosseri
species.intro: Observed hunting fiddler crabs on Kuala Gula mudflats at low tide.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Giant mudskippers live in burrows on estuarine mudflats and emerge at low tide.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Litter can pollute mudflats, but the sources here do not show litter injury to this species at Kuala Gula.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take litter away and avoid trampling the mudflat or burrows.

species.name: Mangrove Crabs
species.subtitle: Crabs · species vary
species.intro: Crabs are listed in Kilim’s mangrove ecosystem; the guide does not identify one species here.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Different crab species live among mangrove roots and tidal mud in Kilim.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Crabs in other mangroves have taken in human-made microparticles; no Kilim-specific harm is shown here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Remove reachable litter without damaging roots or handling crabs.

species.credit: Tracy Enright, U.S. Geological Survey · Public Domain

species.name: Painted Terrapin
species.subtitle: Batagur borneoensis
species.intro: Recorded in the Setiu wetland and coastal complex.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Painted terrapins use Setiu’s coastal wetlands and nesting beaches.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: No source here documents a painted terrapin harmed by litter at Setiu.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep nesting shores clean and leave terrapins and nests undisturbed.

species.name: Southern River Terrapin
species.subtitle: Batagur affinis
species.intro: Recorded in Sungai Setiu and Sungai Chalok.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Southern river terrapins live in large rivers and estuaries and nest on river sandbanks.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Pollution can damage their habitat, but the cited account does not document litter injury at Setiu.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep riverbanks clean and do not disturb nesting sandbanks.

species.credit: Photo · Mohd Hafiz Noor Shams · CC BY 2.5

species.name: Estuarine Crocodile
species.subtitle: Crocodylus porosus
species.intro: Recorded in Kuching Wetlands’ 2005 Ramsar designation information.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Estuarine crocodiles use tidal rivers and mangroves, including Kuching Wetlands.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic was found in crocodile stomachs elsewhere in Sarawak; this is not a Kuching Wetlands finding.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Report litter from a safe distance; never enter the water or approach a crocodile to clean up.

species.name: Tube-Dwelling Worm
species.subtitle: Diopatra claparedii
species.intro: Collected from Morib mudflat tubes and studied for nervous-system regeneration.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This tube-dwelling worm was sampled in Morib’s intertidal mudflat.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Related worms can encounter microplastics, but the Morib study did not test this worm for litter effects.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic off mudflats and leave worm tubes undisturbed.

species.credit: Wibowo et al. (2025), Figure 1 · CC BY-SA 4.0

species.name: Bakau Kurap
species.subtitle: Rhizophora mucronata
species.intro: The Kilim park guide lists this tree as a dominant mangrove.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Bakau kurap is one of the main mangrove trees in Kilim’s tidal forest.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic can accumulate in mangroves, but no damage to this tree at Kilim is documented here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep waste out of mangroves and do not damage the roots.

species.name: Nipa Palm
species.subtitle: Nypa fruticans
species.intro: The Kilim guide lists this palm in scattered swamp-forest stands.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Nipa palms grow in scattered stands in Kilim’s swamp forest.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Litter threatens mangrove habitats generally, but this source does not show harm to Kilim’s nipa palms.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take litter away without cutting or trampling the plants.

species.name: Rhizophora apiculata
species.subtitle: Mangrove tree
species.intro: The most densely recorded tree in a surveyed Matang forest strip.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This mangrove was the most abundant tree in the studied Matang forest stands.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic pollution threatens mangrove forests, but no Matang-specific injury to this species is shown.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep rubbish out of tidal channels and protect the roots.

species.name: Bruguiera parviflora
species.subtitle: Mangrove tree
species.intro: The second most densely recorded tree in the same Matang survey.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This mangrove was recorded in the studied Matang forest stands.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic can build up in mangroves, but no Matang-specific injury to this tree is shown.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Remove accessible rubbish without disturbing young mangroves.

species.name: Enhalus acoroides
species.subtitle: Seagrass
species.intro: Researchers planted its seedlings at Merambong during habitat recovery.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This seagrass grows in Sungai Pulai estuary and was used in a restoration study.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Debris occurs in seagrass meadows, but that study did not show litter damage to this species.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep rubbish out of the water and do not trample seagrass.

species.name: Halophila ovalis
species.subtitle: Seagrass
species.intro: Included as ground cover in Sungai Pulai seagrass recovery plots.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This low-growing seagrass forms cover within Sungai Pulai’s seagrass meadow.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Debris can collect in seagrass habitat, but no local litter damage to this species is documented here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep the shallows clean and avoid stepping on seagrass.

species.credit: Photo · Dr Catherine Collier (James Cook University), TropWATER · CC BY 3.0 AU · resized; displayed crop

species.name: Thalassia hemprichii
species.subtitle: Seagrass
species.intro: Recorded in seagrass communities across the Sungai Pulai estuary.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This seagrass is recorded in Sungai Pulai estuary’s mixed meadow.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Seagrass meadows can trap debris, but the local study did not document damage to this species.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take waste home and avoid trampling the meadow.

species.name: Halodule pinifolia
species.subtitle: Seagrass
species.intro: The most abundant seagrass in a 2009–2010 Lawas survey.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This seagrass was the most abundant species in the Lawas survey.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Microplastics were found on this species in Sri Lanka, but Lawas survey did not measure litter effects.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic out of shallow water and avoid trampling seagrass.

species.credit: Photo · Joselito Balbosa Chavez, Jr. · CC BY-NC 4.0

species.name: Blood Cockle
species.intro: Pantai Remis samples showed microplastics in a 2024 study.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Blood cockles live in soft tidal mud; samples were studied at Pantai Remis.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Microplastics were detected in local samples, but effects on those animals were not measured.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Reduce plastic waste and join safe shore cleanups.

species.name: Shorebirds
species.intro: A local guide records shorebirds at Pantai Redang without naming species.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Shorebirds feed and rest on beaches and tidal flats; a guide lists them at Pantai Redang.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Litter can harm coastal birds, but these sources identify no injured bird or Redang species.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep the shore litter-free and give resting birds space.

species.credit: Photo · Kentish plover, a shorebird example · Nepenthes · CC BY-SA 3.0 · resized; displayed crop

species.name: Macaques
species.intro: Documented around Monkey Beach; the guide does not identify a species.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Macaques live around the forested coast near Monkey Beach.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Food litter can attract macaques, but no injury at Monkey Beach is documented here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Secure food and rubbish; never feed or touch macaques.

species.name: Black Sea Cucumber
species.subtitle: Holothuria leucospilota · linked record
species.intro: Collected at Teluk Nipah in November 2011.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This seafloor invertebrate was collected at Teluk Nipah in November 2011.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Microplastics affected larvae in an experiment, but pollution was not measured at Teluk Nipah.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic out of water and leave sea cucumbers where they are.

species.name: Sea Cucumber
species.subtitle: Stichopus horrens · linked Pangkor record
species.intro: Collected at Pangkor Laut in 2011, not specifically Emerald Bay.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This sea cucumber was collected at Pangkor Laut, not specifically Emerald Bay.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: A later study found microplastics in this species around Pulau Pangkor, not in the 2011 individual.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep litter out of coastal water and do not remove sea cucumbers.

species.name: Hawksbill Turtle
species.subtitle: Eretmochelys imbricata
species.intro: Nesting records exist at Malaysian coastal sites; the record is not a current sighting.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Hawksbills use coral reefs and nest on sandy coasts, including Malaysian sites.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic and lost gear can harm hawksbills, but these records show no locally injured turtle.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep nesting beaches clear of litter and do not disturb turtles or nests.

species.name: Faunus Snail
species.subtitle: Faunus ater
species.intro: Collected at Pantai Bisikan Bayu in a 2007 study.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: This brackish-water snail was collected at Pantai Bisikan Bayu in 2007.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: That study measured heavy metals, not plastic litter; no local litter effect is documented.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep rubbish off tidal mud and leave living snails undisturbed.

species.name: Horseshoe Crab
species.intro: Spawning was recorded at Pantai Balok during 2009–2013.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Horseshoe crabs spawn on the sandy shore at Balok.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: A local study reported crabs tangled in crab nets but did not say the nets were abandoned.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Report lost nets and keep spawning sand clear without handling crabs.

species.name: Clownfish
species.intro: Clownfish shelter among sea anemones. This card does not identify a species.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Clownfish live with host anemones in shallow reef habitats. This card does not establish a local species record.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Marine debris can damage reef habitat, but no injured clownfish is documented at this location.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep litter out of the sea and do not touch anemones or reefs.

species.credit: Photo · Ocellaris clownfish · Zoltán Stekkelpak · CC0 1.0

species.name: Corals
species.intro: Corals are animals. Many reef-building kinds create shelter for marine life.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Corals live in marine reef habitats. This card does not identify a coral species or a beach survey.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Nets and other debris can smother, scrape, or break corals; no local damage is documented by this card.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Never stand on coral. Report large tangled gear rather than pulling it off yourself.

sources.label: Malaysia Travel Guide · Pulau Kapas photo

species.credit: Photo · Existing Pulau Kapas card · source below

species.name: Seagrass
species.intro: Seagrasses are rooted, flowering marine plants that form underwater meadows.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Seagrasses grow on the seabed in shallow coastal waters. This card does not identify a species.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Lost gear can shade, scrape, or crush seagrass, but this card does not document local damage.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep waste out of the water and avoid walking on seagrass beds.

species.credit: Photo · Enhalus acoroides · Christian Gloor · CC BY 2.0

species.name: Mangroves
species.intro: Mangroves are coastal plants that form tidal forests and support marine life.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: They grow along sheltered tidal coasts and estuaries. This card does not identify a species.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic can collect in mangroves and harm the ecosystem; no local tree injury is recorded here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take litter away without damaging roots or seedlings.

species.credit: Photo · Bakau kurap mangrove · Shagil Kannur · CC BY-SA 3.0

species.name: Sea Turtles
species.intro: Sea turtles use marine waters and return to land to nest. This card does not name a species.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Sea turtles live at sea, and females nest on beaches. Exact habitats vary by species.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Sea turtles can ingest debris; no local injured turtle is shown on this card.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take beach litter home and observe turtles and nests from a distance.

species.credit: Photo supplied by the project team · sea-turtle group example

species.name: Morib Scaleworm
species.subtitle: Grubeulepis malayensis
species.intro: A small scaleworm first described from specimens collected at Morib Beach.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: It was found in empty tubes made by another worm on Morib’s sandy shore; a wider range is not established here.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: The Morib study did not test how plastic litter affects this species.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep the shore clean and leave worm tubes undisturbed.

species.credit: Original schematic · Radar Pantai · CC BY 4.0 · based on the morphology described by Nishi (2001); not a photograph or an identification guide

species.name: Mud Lobster
species.subtitle: Thalassina kelanang
species.intro: A mud lobster species described from Kelanang Beach.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Researchers collected it from burrow mounds inside or near Kelanang’s mangrove fringe in 2006–2007.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: The species description did not measure litter exposure or harm; its collection net is not evidence of discarded gear.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep litter off mangrove mud and avoid disturbing burrow mounds.

species.credit: Specimen photo · Moh H. H. & Chong V. C. (2009), Figure 1 · CC BY 4.0 via Plazi / Zenodo · resized; displayed crop

species.name: Indo-Pacific Finless Porpoise
species.subtitle: Neophocaena phocaenoides · regional record
species.intro: A small coastal porpoise recorded in Kuching Bay surveys, without a documented Damai Beach sighting.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: The linked survey recorded this species in Kuching Bay’s coastal waters during 2010–2011.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Fishing gear ingestion was documented elsewhere, but the Kuching Bay survey reports no local litter injury.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Report lost gear and watch porpoises from a distance.

species.credit: Photo · portioid / iNaturalist · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Hong Kong specimen · resized; displayed crop

species.name: Syringodium isoetifolium
species.subtitle: Seagrass · Teluk Kemang record
species.intro: A seagrass recorded at Teluk Kemang in a Port Dickson survey.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: It grows in shallow coastal water; the surveyed Teluk Kemang site was a rocky intertidal shore.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Derelict gear can damage seagrass beds, but the survey did not measure damage to this species there.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep waste out of the water and avoid trampling seagrass.

species.credit: Photo · Philippe Bourjon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · resized; displayed crop

species.name: Rhizophora stylosa
species.subtitle: Mangrove tree · Bagan Lalang record
species.intro: A mangrove tree documented on Bagan Lalang’s seafront in March 2012.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Researchers found scattered trees on seafront sand flats and in mixed stands farther inland.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Plastic threatens mangrove habitats, but the survey did not document litter injury to these trees.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep rubbish out of mangroves without damaging roots or seedlings.

species.credit: Photo · CRCHF · CC BY-SA 3.0 · resized; displayed crop

species.name: Coastal Shellfish
species.subtitle: Blood cockles & clams · group record
species.intro: A Pantai Remis study examined blood cockles and other coastal clams; this card covers several shellfish.
species.evidence: From published sources · not a live sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: These shellfish live in coastal sediments. The study sampled them at Pantai Remis, Jeram; exact habitats differ by species.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Microplastics were detected in the local samples, but the study did not measure harm to those animals.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Reduce plastic waste and join safe shore cleanups.

species.credit: Photo · Nick Hobgood · CC BY-SA 3.0 · giant clam, representative shellfish group example

species.name: Irrawaddy Dolphin
species.subtitle: Lumba-lumba Irrawaddy · Orcaella brevirostris
species.intro: A round head and no beak. Lives close to shore.
species.evidence: Published evidence · not a local sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Irrawaddy dolphins use shallow coastal waters and river mouths.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Entanglement in fishing nets is documented; no local injured dolphin is shown, and active nets are not necessarily litter.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Report lost nets and watch dolphins from a distance.

species.name: Moorish Idol
species.subtitle: Zanclus cornutus
species.intro: Long white fin and bold black bands. Grazes on reef sponges.
species.evidence: Published evidence · not a local sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Moorish idols inhabit lagoons, reef flats, and rocky or coral reefs.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Marine litter can harm reef habitats, but no species-specific or local injury record is shown here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take your litter away and do not step on coral.

species.name: Ocellaris Clownfish
species.subtitle: Ikan badut · Amphiprion ocellaris
species.intro: Shelters in sea anemones and rarely strays far from them.
species.evidence: Published evidence · not a local sighting

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Ocellaris clownfish live among sea anemones on shallow coral reefs.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Lab-reared juveniles ingested microplastics, but this does not show harm at this reef.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic out of the sea and avoid touching anemones or corals.

texts: A Matang survey found riverside Rhizophora stands changing into mixed mangrove forest farther inland.
Species of this habitat · not local sightings
Observed hunting fiddler crabs on Kuala Gula’s mudflats at low tide.
This was the most densely recorded tree in the surveyed forest strip.
This was the second most densely recorded tree in the same survey.

habitats.title: Sungai Pulai Seagrass
habitats.intro: Sungai Pulai’s estuary contains seagrass shoals where researchers monitored plant communities and tested habitat recovery.
texts: Sungai Pulai’s estuary contains seagrass shoals where researchers monitored plant communities and tested habitat recovery.
Species of this habitat · not local sightings
Researchers planted its seedlings at Merambong to help stabilise sediment during habitat recovery.
This species was included as ground cover in the study’s seagrass recovery plots.
This species appears in the study’s records of seagrass communities across the estuary.
Keep litter out of coastal habitats.
Monitoring covered 2015–2025 at selected estuary shoals, not every location within Sungai Pulai.

habitats.title: Setiu Wetlands
habitats.intro: A connected lagoon, river and mangrove landscape supports terrapins and turtle nesting along parts of the Setiu coast.
texts: A connected lagoon, river and mangrove landscape supports terrapins and turtle nesting along parts of the Setiu coast.

Recorded in the Setiu wetland and coastal complex.
Nests along parts of Setiu’s sandy coast.
Recorded in Sungai Setiu and Sungai Chalok.
Keep litter out of coastal habitats.
Setiu complex; sources from 2016 and 2022, with current sightings unverified.

habitats.title: Lawas Seagrass
habitats.intro: Historical surveys recorded diverse seagrasses across sampled intertidal meadows on the Lawas coast.
texts: Historical surveys recorded diverse seagrasses across sampled intertidal meadows on the Lawas coast.
Species of this habitat · not local sightings
The most abundant seagrass in the 2009–2010 survey.
One of the species recorded at sampled coastal sites.
Recorded within the surveyed intertidal meadow.

Sampled Lawas coast; surveyed June 2009–May 2010 and published in 2013.

habitats.title: Morib Mudflat
habitats.intro: Researchers collected tube-dwelling marine worms from sandy mud at an intertidal site they identified as Morib.
texts: Researchers collected tube-dwelling marine worms from sandy mud at an intertidal site they identified as Morib.
Species of this habitat · not local sightings
Collected from mudflat tubes, this worm was studied for its ability to regenerate its nervous system.
Published in 2021, this records one collection site; the collection date and present population remain unverified.
